discussion.body:
We have made the game-engine / graphics production decision for Asteria.
Asteria is targeting an **Octopath Traveler-style HD-2D presentation**: 2D pixel-art characters integrated into real-time 3D environments with lighting, shadows, depth of field, particles, post-processing, and cinematic camera work.
Use the following decisions for the Windows 11 Astra development VM.
### PRIMARY ENGINE
Install:
**Unreal Engine 5.8**
Install it through the **Epic Games Launcher**.
Asteria should now be built around Unreal rather than Godot.
The intended architecture is:
* Unreal Engine 5.8 * 3D environments * 2D sprite characters * Paper 2D for sprites / Flipbooks * Blueprint for gameplay iteration and content scripting * C++ for core systems, reusable architecture, performance-sensitive systems, and Astra-generated code * Sequencer for cinematics, camera work, scripted scenes, and presentation * Niagara for effects * Unreal lighting/post-processing for the HD-2D appearance
Do not install Unity.
Do not make Godot part of the primary Asteria development stack unless we specifically decide later to maintain a comparison prototype.
### UNREAL PLUGINS / FEATURES
Once Unreal is installed, enable these built-in systems for the Asteria project:
* Paper 2D * Niagara * Sequencer / Level Sequence * Enhanced Input * Modeling Tools Editor Mode
Paper 2D is specifically important because Asteria will combine sprite characters with Unreal's 3D world.
### VISUAL STUDIO
Install:
**Visual Studio 2026 Community**
During Visual Studio installation enable:
* Game development with C++ * Desktop development with C++ * .NET desktop development * Visual Studio Tools for Unreal Engine * C++ profiling tools * C++ AddressSanitizer * Windows 11 SDK
Use the current MSVC toolchain recommended for Unreal 5.8.
Visual Studio will be the primary C++ IDE for Asteria.
Do not substitute VS Code as the primary Unreal C++ environment.
### 3D CONTENT SOFTWARE
Install:
**Blender 5.2 LTS**
Blender will be Asteria's primary 3D DCC application for:
* environment geometry * buildings * props * terrain assets * collision meshes * UV work * material-supporting assets * FBX/glTF export into Unreal
Use the LTS branch rather than experimental Blender releases.
### PIXEL / SPRITE SOFTWARE
Install:
**Aseprite 1.3.18.3 or newer stable 1.3.x**
Aseprite will be the primary sprite-production application for:
* character sprites * sprite animation * sprite sheets * combat animation * NPC animation * pixel effects where appropriate * palette work
Export sprite assets primarily as PNG/sprite sheets for Unreal Paper 2D.
### SOURCE CONTROL
Install:
**Git for Windows 2.55 or newer**
Also configure:
**Git LFS**
Run:
git lfs install
Asteria will use Git/GitHub + Git LFS rather than Perforce at this stage.
Git LFS will eventually track large/binary game-development assets such as:
* .uasset * .umap * .blend * large textures * audio * source-art assets
Do not initialize the Unreal repository yet unless we are specifically at the project-creation step. We will create the .gitignore and .gitattributes deliberately for Unreal.
### PYTHON
Python is already installed and working in the VM.
Keep it.
Python will be used for Astra automation, asset-pipeline scripts, validation, build helpers, and development tooling.
### EXISTING DEVELOPMENT STORAGE
The shared/project drive is already:
Z:\Astra-Dev
Continue using this as the main development workspace unless Unreal performs poorly when projects are run directly from the VirtualBox shared drive.
If Unreal has file-locking, compilation, DerivedDataCache, or performance problems on Z:, create the active Unreal project on the VM's local virtual SSD and use Z: for interchange/backups/tools instead.
Do not move anything yet unless testing shows this is necessary.
### IMPORTANT VIRTUALBOX GRAPHICS CONFIGURATION
This VM uses VirtualBox.
Before relying on Unreal rendering, confirm:
* Guest Additions installed — already complete * Graphics Controller = VBoxSVGA * Enable 3D Acceleration = ON * Video Memory = maximum available
VirtualBox currently exposes only Direct3D 11/11.1-class graphics to modern Windows guests.
Therefore, initially configure the Asteria Unreal prototype around:
* DirectX 11 / Shader Model 5 where necessary * no dependency on Lumen * no dependency on Nanite * conventional Unreal lighting * point lights / spot lights / directional lights * shadows * post processing * depth of field * bloom * fog * Niagara effects
This is acceptable for the initial Asteria HD-2D prototype because the original Octopath Traveler achieved its look in Unreal Engine 4 without UE5's Lumen or Nanite.
We should NOT design Asteria around Lumen or Nanite until Unreal has been tested on this VM.
If VirtualBox becomes the limiting factor, we will address the rendering environment separately rather than changing the game-engine decision.
### INITIAL PROJECT DECISION
When we reach Unreal project creation, use:
* Games project * C++ project * Blueprint available for gameplay/content logic * Desktop target * Windows first * no mobile target * 3D environment + Paper 2D sprite architecture
Do not create the Unreal project yet unless that is the next instructed step.
### CURRENT INSTALLATION ORDER
Proceed in this order:
1. Git for Windows + Git LFS 2. Epic Games Launcher 3. Unreal Engine 5.8 4. Visual Studio 2026 Community with Unreal/C++ workloads 5. Blender 5.2 LTS 6. Aseprite 7. Verify Unreal launches successfully inside the VM 8. Test a minimal 3D scene with one Paper 2D sprite, lighting, shadows, and depth of field 9. Only after that test succeeds, create the permanent Asteria project structure
The immediate goal is to get the **Astra Windows VM capable of producing an Octopath-style Unreal HD-2D prototype**, not to start building the game yet.
